designVerdict: SELECTED - the Figure 6 'Voltage Regulator' block, now identified
notes: THIS IS THE UNLABELLED BOX. Hynetek publishes the Figure 6 'Voltage Regulator' with values at https://www.hynetek.com/2730.html - never in the datasheet. It is a BSS138 SOURCE FOLLOWER: gate pulled up through 10 kOhm and clamped by a 28 V Zener, source feeding the HUSB238A VBUS pin. A 0 Ohm link (RJ2 in their reference) bypasses it for builds at 28 V or below.

A source follower, NOT the resistor-plus-Zener shunt assumed earlier. The distinction matters: a follower holds the pin at roughly (Vgate - Vth) with low output impedance, whereas a series resistor would drop voltage with load current.

FOLLOWER DROP RESOLVED, two parts. (1) HUSB238A VDD (pin 5) is an INPUT supply, not an output - p.4 recommends tying it to a 3.3 V rail - which drops the VBUS-pin requirement from 4.5 V to 3.15 V and its draw from 4.5 mA to 800 uA. (2) D14 (RB751V-40, C7502691) from the 5 V rail to the VBUS pin holds it at 4.13 V on a 4.75 V bus. This part's Vgs was never the thing to fix; the pin's requirement was.

Residual: two 4.0 V thresholds sit just under the 4.13 V delivered - VBUS_OK rising (vVBPRS_R, 3.67/4.0/4.4 V min/typ/max, p.6) and the under-voltage detector (vVBUV_F1, 80% of a 5 V RDO). Both have 0.13 V of margin on typical parts and neither is guaranteed at the corner. An earlier note called 3.67 V the typical; it is the minimum. The lever if it fails is the 5 V rail, which sits at its own dropout floor, not the diode.
